article_manifest.title: Two European Women Freed After Kidnap in Niger
article_manifest.original_title: Two European Women Freed After Kidnap in Niger
article_manifest.summary: A Swiss woman and an Austrian woman kidnapped in Niger in 2025 have been released after spending more than a year in captivity, their respective governments have confirmed. The women, identified as 69-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Austrian citizen Eva Gretzmacher, arrived in Benghazi, eastern Libya, following their release, according to local media reports.

Austria's Eva Gretzmacher and Switzerland's Claudia Abbt thank Haftar father and son in the video below, broadcast by al-Masar TV, a Benghazi TV, on platform X .

article_manifest.summary: The dialogue initiated in Dakar on 17 October should provide a sustainable framework for relations between the ESA and ECOWAS. The movement of people, trade and security call for concrete commitments between the two sets. Institutional separation has not erased interdependencies Since the effective withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, the countries of both sets continue to share trade corridors, population movements and security challenges.

article_manifest.title: Swiss and Austrian women in Libya after release from Niger kidnap ordeal
article_manifest.original_title: Swiss and Austrian women in Libya after release from Niger kidnap ordeal
article_manifest.summary: An Austrian and a Swiss women kidnapped in Niger more than a year and a half ago have been freed and are in Libya, Bern and Vienna announced Thursday. Sixty-nine-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Eva Gretzmacher arrived in the eastern city of Benghazi where they received medical treatment. Their release follows an intervention by Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, who controls the east and parts of the south of the country.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: Shooting, lethal injection, hanging... details of the procedure for executing the death penalty
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : Fusillade, injection létale, pendaison… les détails de la procédure d’exécution de la peine de mort
article_manifest.summary: The new Burkinabe Criminal Code provides for the reinstatement of the death penalty for several serious crimes and specifies the modalities of its execution. The innovations of the text, four modes of execution are planned: shooting, lethal injection, hanging and electrocution. The system also provides a framework for remedies and the case of pregnant convicted women Adopted unanimously by the 71 voters of the People's Legislative Assembly (Alp) on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the new Penal Code marks an important development in Burkina Faso's criminal law.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty as Junta Tightens Grip
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty as Junta Tightens Grip
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso's unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code restoring the death penalty for offences including high treason, terrorism, espionage, parricide and importing expired or prohibited products. The death penalty for ordinary crimes was abolished in 2018. Human Rights Watch warns that reinstating capital punishment could further threaten civil liberties under the military junta, which took power in a 2022 coup.

article_manifest.title: Two former European hostages kidnapped in Niger in 2025 have been released and are in Libya
article_manifest.original_title: Deux ex-otages européennes enlevées au Niger en 2025 ont été libérées et se trouvent en Libye
article_manifest.summary: Eva Gretzmacher and Claudia Abbt, two European women kidnapped in the Sahel in 2025, are free, a Libyan television channel has announced. The announcement was confirmed Thursday, October 22 thanks to images of the two ex-hostages who arrived in Benghazi Because it was through the strong man of eastern Libya, Marshal Khalifa Haftar, that they regained their freedom.

article_manifest.title: Read more: Swiss and Austrian hostages freed in Niger
article_manifest.original_title: Read more: Swiss and Austrian hostages freed in Niger
article_manifest.summary: Swiss and Austrian hostages freed in Niger Two European nationals, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman, who were kidnapped in Niger over a year ago, have been released. They have arrived in Benghazi, in eastern Libya, a local television channel announced during the night between Wednesday and Thursday. “Two hostages, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman, have been released after a year and a half in captivity in Niger and have arrived in Benghazi thanks to the intervention of the Deputy Commander-in-Chief,” Saddam Haftar, deputy commander-in-chief of Libya’s armed forces, said Libyan television Al-Masar announced.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso: The main innovations of the new Penal Code
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso : Les principales innovations du nouveau Code pénal
article_manifest.summary: The new Burkina Faso Penal Code adopted on 20 October 2026 by the People's Legislative Assembly introduces a dozen main innovations including the reinstatement of the death penalty for certain offences, the revision of financial sanctions related to the misappropriation of public funds, the creation of new offences and the raising of certain penalties. The amendments also concern road traffic, the environment, international crimes, protected animals and offences committed using information and communication technologies.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men, according to security and local sources
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés, selon des sources sécuritaires et locales
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks by armed men in the Menaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacement, several security, local and associative sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arrived on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, came.
